extracted.intended_audience: SNAP applicants and recipients (people seeking or receiving SNAP benefits)
extracted.subtask_description: Federal guidance describing SNAP general work requirements and the ABAWD (able-bodied adult without dependents) work requirement and time limit, including who must comply, how to meet requirements, excused categories, and consequences for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of general work requirements (age 16–59 and able to work)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are age 16–59 and able to work, you will probably need to meet the general work requirements to get SNAP benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General work requirements apply to most people in this age and ability range; they determine whether additional duties (registration, participation, accepting work) are required to maintain eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: General work requirements (register, participate, accept work, maintain hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: The general work requirements include registering for work, participating in SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) or workfare if assigned by your state SNAP agency, taking a suitable job if offered, and not voluntarily quitting a job or reducing your work hours below 30 a week without a good reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State agencies may assign E&T or workfare; 'suitable job' and 'good reason' are determinations made by the state. Failure to comply with these elements triggers sanctions (see consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from the general work requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You are excused from the general work requirements if you are any one of these things: already working at least 30 hours a week (or earning wages at least equal to the federal minimum wage multiplied by 30 hours); meeting work requirements for another program (TANF or unemployment compensation); taking care of a child under six or an incapacitated person; unable to work due to a physical or mental limitation; participating regularly in an alcohol or drug treatment program; studying in school or a training program at least half-time (but college students are subject to other eligibility rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed condition independently excuses a person from general work requirements. College students may have additional, separate eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failing to meet general work requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have to meet the general work requirements but you don’t, you are disqualified from getting SNAP for at least a month and must start meeting the requirements to get SNAP again. If you get back on SNAP and then don’t meet the requirements again, then you are disqualified for longer than a month and you could be disqualified forever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions escalate with repeated failures to comply; initial sanction is at least one-month disqualification, with longer or permanent disqualification possible on subsequent failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of ABAWD work requirement and time limit (age 18–54, able to work, no dependents)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are age 18–54, able to work, and don’t have any dependents, you might need to meet both the general work requirements and an additional work requirement for ABAWDs to get SNAP for more than three months in three years (the time limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABAWD rules are an additional layer on top of the general requirements; the time limit restricts receipt of SNAP to three months in any rolling three-year period unless the ABAWD requirement is met or an exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to meet the ABAWD work requirement (80 hours/month or assigned workfare)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can meet the ABAWD work requirement by doing any one of these things: Work at least 80 hours a month (work can be for pay, for goods or services (for something other than money), unpaid, or as a volunteer); participate in a work program at least 80 hours a month (a work program could be SNAP E&T or another federal, state, or local work program); participate in a combination of work and work program hours for a total of at least 80 hours a month; participate in workfare for the number of hours assigned to you each month (the number of hours will depend on the amount of your SNAP benefit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work includes paid, in-kind, unpaid, or volunteer efforts; hours in eligible work programs count; combinations of activities can be aggregated to reach 80 hours; workfare hours are set based on benefit amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from ABAWD work requirement and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: You are excused from the ABAWD work requirement and time limit if you are any one of these things: unable to work due to a physical or mental limitation; pregnant; have someone under 18 in your SNAP household; excused from the general work requirements (see above); a veteran; experiencing homelessness; age 24 or younger and in foster care on your 18th birthday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any single listed condition grants exemption from the ABAWD time limit and requirement. Being excused from the general work requirements also exempts you from ABAWD rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and requalification after ABAWD time-limit failure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have to meet the ABAWD work requirement but you don’t, you will lose your benefits after three months. To get SNAP again, you must meet the ABAWD work requirement for a 30-day period or become excused. Otherwise, you need to wait until the end of your three-year period, when you’ll get another three months under the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of benefits occurs after three months of noncompliance within the applicable 3-year period; re-entry requires meeting the requirement for 30 consecutive days or obtaining an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) and workfare as compliance mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) or other assigned work programs (including workfare) can satisfy general or ABAWD work requirements when assigned by the state SNAP agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State agencies may assign E&T or workfare; participation hours in these programs count toward the 80-hour ABAWD threshold and toward general participation requirements as specified by the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upcoming legislative changes affecting ABAWD exceptions and waivers (One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 changes the work requirements for SNAP able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs). This includes changes to the ABAWD exception criteria and ABAWD waiver criteria. We will update this page once the guidance is released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current rules are subject to change pending federal guidance implementing the Act; recipients should monitor updates for revised exemption/waiver criteria and procedures.
